title: The Almsgiving
logline: A family has been up since before dawn to cook for the monks. One person arranges every plate beautifully, one checks for mistakes, one waits to be told, one keeps drifting off to talk, and one quietly wonders whether any of it matters.

object.note: Object 4 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The worn circle of habit moves indoors: a household up before dawn for an almsgiving, each person finding a different way through the same work.

thread_out.thread: Different temperaments in one kitchen become different stages in one workshop: apprentices at every level beside a carver who still calls themselves a learner.

lesson.in_simple_terms: People doing the same work go about it in very different ways. The texts say everyone has every leaning, with each person tilting a little one way, and that each troublesome leaning sits close to a good one.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: එකම වැඩේ කරන අය එය කරන්නේ වෙනස් වෙනස් විදිහට; හැමෝම තුළ හැම ගතියක්ම තිබුණත්, එක් එක් කෙනා එක් එක් පැත්තකට ටිකක් නැඹුරු වෙයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma describes six temperaments (carita): greedy, hating, deluded, faithful, intelligent and speculative. Margaya stresses that temperament is simply a person's nature and that, because everyone has all these qualities, it is very hard to tell which one leads. Each troublesome leaning resembles a good one: greed is close to faith, hatred to intelligence, and delusion to speculative thinking. Margaya also notes that good done while doubting whether good bears fruit is not strong good.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Through one long night and dawn in the kitchen, the camera simply watches how each person handles the same tasks: one arranging every plate beautifully, one checking for mistakes, one waiting to be told, one drifting off to talk. The viewer recognises people they know, and themselves, in how each one works. If a family member voices a quiet doubt, the film lets it sit beside the offering without taking sides.

key_terms.en: temperament; a person's nature or dominant leaning

lesson.caution: This is not a personality test: no family member is presented as a type, and the texts' signs of temperament are guidance for a meditation teacher, not a way to profile people on camera.
lesson.builds_on: The tether showed that everyone goes round some circle; the almsgiving shows that each person's circle has its own shape, even inside the same kitchen.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
